tasks.short: Consult specialist colleagues to test the legal basis for proceedings.

steps.what: Define the legal question and identify the relevant specialist.
Assemble key facts, disputed points and supporting sources.

loop.input: Consultation scope and authorised matter documents.
loop.output: Consultation brief with source references and unresolved questions.
loop.check: Check source links, distinguish allegations from established facts, and have the lawyer review completeness.
loop.stop: One draft and one correction pass; missing evidence returns to the lawyer.
loop.why_not_simpler: Templates organise the brief, but disputed facts and specialist questions require reading varied text.

steps.what: Share the brief and arrange a consultation.
Challenge assumptions, discuss competing interpretations and test procedural options.
Decide which legal grounds and further checks to pursue.
File the conclusion and assign agreed follow-up actions.

tasks.design: A consultation form in the {WORKFLOW} selects authorised documents from the {DOCS} and generates a source-linked brief using a bounded drafting loop. The lawyer approves the brief, while the {CALENDAR} handles availability and the {PROJECT} records agreed actions; specialist discussion and legal conclusions remain human.
tasks.previous_blocker: Useful preparation depended on reading scattered matter documents. Scheduling could already be configured, but document access and consistent matter identifiers often needed separate work.
tasks.enabler_now: AI-assisted coding reduces the effort of building document connectors and brief templates. Bounded drafting can organise free text for review without taking over the consultation.
tasks.still_hard: Specialist disagreement, incomplete facts and privilege boundaries remain difficult. Confidential access must follow the matter, including when specialists work outside the company.
tasks.human_edge: Knowing which assumption to challenge and recognising when a colleague's qualified answer changes the case.

ambition.what: A pre-proceedings specialist challenge clinic for borderline disputes.

tasks.altitude: The lawyer spends less time assembling briefs and arranging meetings, with more room to test weak arguments early. Authority over proceedings and spend does not change.

reach.task: Prepare a source-linked issue chronology for specialist consultation.
reach.learn: Evidence provenance, privilege marking and separating disputed facts from legal questions.

evidence.claim: Research, drafting and document review capabilities exist today; this does not establish automated specialist judgement.
Scheduling and recording agreed actions can use configured workflows without a model.
Dutch professional guidance requires confidentiality safeguards, citation checks and continuing lawyer responsibility.

assumptions: The baseline is a legal team in a company with 200 to 2,000 staff.
Automated invitations cover internal specialists selected by the lawyer; external sharing requires recipient and access review.
Time shares, remaining effort and build ranges are planning estimates, not measured outcomes.
Access estimates include privilege review and any employee consultation required by national rules.
The conversation remains the largest step, consistent with the supplied priors.
unknowns: Which specialist directory and matter access controls the team uses.
Whether consultation records may be processed by an approved model service.
Who may share matter material with external specialists.
Which national professional and employee consultation rules apply.
research_questions: Can brief generation preserve document-level permissions and reliable page references?
Which omissions in historical consultation briefs most often changed specialist advice?
new_work: Review generated briefs for missing adverse facts and misleading summaries.
Maintain specialist routing and consultation templates.
Resolve access failures and remove outdated matter links.

tasks.short: Examine legal records to establish ownership or support a legal opinion.

steps.what: Define the ownership question, relevant entities, jurisdiction and search period.
Search registry and legal research portals; obtain relevant records.
Read records and trace ownership, dates, restrictions and gaps.

loop.input: Retrieved records with registry identifiers, dates and source locations.
loop.output: Evidence table and chronology, with missing links and conflicting entries.
loop.check: Validate identifiers and dates; link each extracted statement to its source; review material ownership links.
loop.stop: Process the scoped record set once, with one retry per failed document; unreadable records go to a person.
loop.why_not_simpler: Structured fields use parsers, but deeds and historical records contain variable prose and scanned text.

steps.what: Resolve conflicting records and decide whether the evidence supports the legal conclusion.
Write the opinion with supporting records, qualifications and unresolved issues.

loop.input: Lawyer's legal position, approved evidence table and opinion template.
loop.output: Draft opinion with source references and explicit qualifications.
loop.check: Check every material assertion against the approved evidence; lawyer checks reasoning and all legal citations.
loop.stop: One draft and one correction pass; unsupported propositions remain flagged for the lawyer.
loop.why_not_simpler: Templates cover standard sections; case-specific explanations require prose grounded in the lawyer's conclusion.

steps.what: Approve and send the opinion to the requesting stakeholder.

tasks.design: A scoped search in the {WORKFLOW} retrieves permitted records from the {GOV_PORTAL} and licensed registry and legal research services in the {OTHER}. Deterministic checks preserve identifiers and retrieval dates, while bounded loops create a source-linked evidence table and draft opinion in the {DOCS}; the lawyer resolves conflicts and authorises release.
tasks.previous_blocker: Records used inconsistent identifiers, scans and separate access arrangements. Retrieval automation could collect documents but could not reliably explain an incomplete ownership chain.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing registry interfaces and document extraction can be combined more cheaply with AI-assisted coding. A bounded model can organise prose while retaining source links and explicit gaps.
tasks.still_hard: Registry access, historical gaps, identity ambiguity and the legal effect of registration vary by jurisdiction. A plausible chronology does not establish valid title.
tasks.human_edge: Deciding what the records legally prove, what they leave uncertain and which qualification the stakeholder must understand.

ambition.what: An early ownership-gap report before transaction terms are negotiated.

tasks.altitude: The lawyer spends more time resolving title defects and advising on transaction conditions. Authority to certify ownership or approve transactions does not expand.

reach.task: Maintain the ownership evidence table and request missing certified records.
reach.learn: Registry provenance, entity matching, document authenticity and escalation of broken ownership links.

evidence.claim: Tabular document review and legal research capabilities are available today; registry coverage needs separate validation.
A documented benchmark found material error rates in legal research tools, supporting source verification.
Structured registry retrieval, identifier checks and retrieval logs can use deterministic integrations.
Where a supplier processes personal data on the company's behalf, GDPR Article 28 governs processor arrangements.

assumptions: The initial build covers one jurisdiction and a defined class of ownership records.
The {OTHER} represents licensed registry and legal research services.
Automated retrieval uses permitted interfaces; paid orders and unavailable records are exceptions for a person.
Remaining time includes reviewing retrieval coverage and extracted material facts.
Time shares, remaining effort and build ranges are planning estimates.
EU data protection requirements apply; access estimates include any consultation required by national rules.
unknowns: Which registries, jurisdictions and record types dominate the team's work.
Whether source licences permit automated retrieval and model processing.
Whether certified records are required for the intended opinions.
How many historical records lack stable identifiers or readable text.
research_questions: Which sources provide authoritative records, stable identifiers and usable retrieval interfaces?
How should the workflow distinguish a negative search result from an incomplete search?
Which ownership claims require direct inspection of the original instrument?
new_work: Review entity matches, missing records and contradictory ownership links.
Maintain registry connectors, licence rules and extraction checks.
Refresh stale records before an opinion is released.
Monitor whether source references remain accessible.

tasks.short: Manage legal matters, deadlines, resources and legal spending.

steps.what: Review new legal requests and determine priority, scope and responsible lawyer.
Create the matter record, document folder and access permissions.
Read notices and enter procedural deadlines and reminders.

loop.output: Candidate trigger date, deadline type and quoted supporting passage.
loop.check: Require lawyer confirmation of trigger facts; calculate dates with versioned jurisdiction rules and holiday calendars.
loop.stop: One extraction and one retry; ambiguity or unsupported rules go to manual deadline entry.
loop.why_not_simpler: Date calculation is deterministic, but identifying the operative event in free-text notices can require reading.

steps.what: Chase matter updates and reconcile the management tracker.
Review capacity, urgent matters and spending; decide assignments and escalations.
Check external counsel invoices against agreed rates, scope and budgets.
Close completed matters and apply document retention instructions.

tasks.design: Configure matter intake and records in the {HELPDESK} and {PROJECT}, linked to permissioned folders in the {DOCS}; replace the duplicate {SPREADSHEET} tracker with live views. A deadline engine proposes dates for lawyer approval, the {BI} shows capacity and spend, and deterministic checks compare invoices in the {ERP} with terms in the {PROCUREMENT}.
tasks.previous_blocker: Matter identifiers, deadlines and invoice references were split across systems and a manually reconciled tracker. Local deadline rules and access permissions made integration more costly than simple reminders.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing forms, permissions and workflow features cover much of the work. AI-assisted coding lowers the effort of connecting records, with a small extraction loop only for unstructured notices.
tasks.still_hard: A wrong procedural trigger can invalidate a correct date calculation. Privilege, legal holds, subjective invoice quality and competing business priorities still need legal judgement.
tasks.human_edge: Allocating scarce legal attention, challenging ineffective external work and escalating risk before a deadline becomes a crisis.

ambition.what: A weekly decision on which legal matters to accelerate, defer or send to external counsel.

tasks.altitude: The legal manager replaces tracker reconciliation with exception review and capacity decisions. Reallocation remains within the existing budget and delegation limits.

reach.task: Run deadline exceptions and matter closure checks.
reach.learn: Procedural trigger validation, access administration and legal hold handling.

reach.task: Investigate external counsel invoice exceptions before lawyer review.
reach.learn: Engagement scope, rate schedules, duplicate detection and the difference between billing errors and legal value.

evidence.claim: Matter records, reminders, status views and rate checks can largely use configuration and deterministic rules.
Document extraction can propose deadline triggers, but procedural validity requires separate legal review.
In the Netherlands, employee monitoring arrangements can engage works-council consent requirements under Article 27.
Processor arrangements for personal data fall under GDPR Article 28.

assumptions: Practice administration is interpreted as corporate legal department operations, including external counsel spending.
The baseline includes a {SPREADSHEET} that reconciles matter updates; this is a scoped assumption, not universal.
The deadline engine initially covers a limited, reviewed set of jurisdiction rules.
Invoice checks use structured billing fields; narrative value judgements remain human.
Closure requires an existing lawyer approval; automation schedules retention without deleting documents.
Access ranges include employee consultation under applicable national rules where reporting affects staff monitoring.
Time shares, remaining effort and build ranges are planning estimates.
unknowns: Whether the company already has a matter-management capability in the {PROJECT} or {OTHER}.
Which deadlines, jurisdictions and holiday calendars must be supported.
Whether counsel invoices carry structured rates, hours and matter identifiers.
Whether reporting measures individual output and requires employee consultation.
Who approves closure, retention exceptions and invoice payment.
research_questions: Which existing system features can replace the tracker without custom development?
What test cases cover service dates, extensions, holidays and conflicting deadline rules?
Can access restrictions carry through to aggregate management reports?
new_work: Maintain versioned deadline rules and regression examples.
Review ambiguous notices and overdue exception queues.
Correct missing matter and invoice identifiers.
Maintain access groups, retention rules and legal holds.
Review whether capacity reporting creates unintended staff monitoring.

tasks.short: Prepare and present a case to the court, responding to questions and opposing arguments.

steps.what: Review the hearing scope, pleadings, evidence and previous court directions.

loop.input: Scoped pleadings, evidence, hearing notice and court directions.
loop.output: Issue map with supporting passages, adverse facts and unresolved points.
loop.check: Resolve every source reference and have the lawyer verify disputed issues against the originals.
loop.stop: One issue map and one correction pass; missing or contradictory evidence stays flagged.
loop.why_not_simpler: Document indexing is deterministic, but identifying contested propositions requires reading varied legal text.

steps.what: Select the argument, concessions and evidence sequence for the hearing.
Draft speaking notes and anticipate questions and opposing arguments.

loop.input: Approved hearing strategy, source-linked issues and selected evidence.
loop.output: Draft speaking notes and anticipated questions with source references.
loop.check: Reject unsupported facts and authorities; lawyer checks citations, concessions and consistency with instructions.
loop.stop: One draft and one correction pass; uncertain legal arguments return to the lawyer.
loop.why_not_simpler: Templates supply structure, but concise arguments and case-specific questions require controlled drafting.

steps.what: Check speaking notes and prepare the indexed hearing bundle.
Present the case and respond to the court, witnesses and opposing counsel.
Record the hearing outcome, new directions and required follow-up.

loop.input: Lawyer's hearing notes and available written court directions.
loop.output: Draft hearing report and proposed follow-up actions.
loop.check: Separate oral recollection from written directions; lawyer verifies commitments and deadline triggers.
loop.stop: One draft and one correction pass; unresolved directions remain unconfirmed and are escalated.
loop.why_not_simpler: A form captures standard fields, but free-text notes need interpretation and concise reporting.

tasks.design: Use the {DOCS} as the controlled evidence base for a bounded issue map and speaking-note generator. Deterministic assembly creates the indexed hearing bundle, and a reviewed report feeds follow-up into the {PROJECT}; the lawyer determines strategy and conducts the hearing.
tasks.previous_blocker: Bundle indexing was already automatable, but producing a reliable case-specific issue map required substantial reading. Unverified drafting could introduce facts or authorities that were absent from the file.
tasks.enabler_now: Source-linked retrieval and bounded drafting make preparation easier to review. AI-assisted coding reduces the cost of combining these capabilities with deterministic bundle checks.
tasks.still_hard: Live advocacy requires credibility, procedural judgement and immediate responses. Citation checks cannot establish that an argument is persuasive or that a concession is authorised.
tasks.human_edge: Reading the court, responding under pressure and choosing when to answer, concede or challenge.

ambition.what: A structured adverse-question rehearsal before significant hearings.

tasks.altitude: The lawyer spends less time indexing evidence and drafting notes, creating room for rehearsal and client preparation. Rights of audience and authority to make concessions do not change.

reach.task: Assemble the hearing bundle and verify every evidence reference.
reach.learn: Court bundle requirements, admissibility flags and tracing statements to original evidence.

reach.task: Record hearing directions and coordinate approved follow-up.
reach.learn: Distinguishing proposed actions from binding directions and escalating uncertain deadlines.

evidence.claim: A firm trial reported 45% time savings on first-draft legal briefings; this is not a hearing-performance result.
Legal research tools have produced incorrect answers in documented testing, so generated authorities require verification.
A documented Dutch case involved costs following unchecked AI-drafted pleadings.
The EU AI Act distinguishes judicial and ADR applications of law to facts; lawyer preparation needs assessment by intended use.

assumptions: The task applies to a lawyer with the necessary rights of audience, including retained external counsel where appropriate.
The baseline is a court hearing; juries are relevant only in jurisdictions and proceedings that use them.
Live presentation remains the largest step, consistent with the supplied priors.
No hearing recording or automatic transcription is assumed.
The lawyer's direct delivery of oral submissions is a human action, so no separate approval gate is added.
Time shares, remaining effort and build ranges are planning estimates.
EU law applies; court procedure, professional duties and employee consultation depend on national rules.
unknowns: Which courts and hearing formats the team uses.
Whether source files contain complete pleadings, exhibits and written directions.
Which bundle formats, filing restrictions and rights of audience apply.
Whether approved processing environments support sensitive litigation data.
research_questions: Can bundle checks detect missing exhibits, inconsistent numbering and broken cross-references?
Which review method catches omitted adverse facts as well as invented assertions?
How should oral directions be reconciled with later written court orders?
new_work: Check generated issue maps for omitted adverse evidence.
Verify every cited authority and material evidence reference.
Maintain bundle templates and court-specific formatting rules.
Review hearing reports before creating commitments or deadline entries.

role.altitude: The lawyer's week shifts from document assembly, searching and status reconciliation toward resolving uncertainty, testing arguments and advising stakeholders. Existing rights to sign, spend, litigate and make concessions remain unchanged unless separately delegated.
reach: Paralegals can maintain source-linked evidence tables and investigate gaps before lawyer review.
Legal assistants can operate matter records, bundle assembly and deadline exception queues.
skills_to_grow: Designing scoped legal questions and source-linked review criteria.
Checking evidence provenance, contradictory records and legal citations.
Translating procedural rules into tested deadline logic.
Managing confidential access, processor arrangements and retention.
Using saved preparation time for specialist challenge and advocacy rehearsal.
role.ambitious_version: A legal team that offers early ownership-gap reports, specialist challenge clinics and adverse-question rehearsals while retaining accountable human legal judgement.
